signals.attribution: Files the agent touched in the preceding turn that the message names; otherwise split evenly over the files it edited in that turn (the 5 most recent).
signals.description: A human prompt that follows agent work and is worded as a correction of it ("No, …", "I told you …", "revert that", "still failing", "you broke …"), corroborated by behaviour: the agent had changed files, and the human names one of them or the agent then changes one of them again. Wording alone, or two weaker cues together, is only a probable correction.
signals.title: User correction
signals.why: Human attention is the most expensive resource in the loop; a correction means the agent's work on these files had to be redirected by hand.

signals.description: The same command line failed 3 or more times in a row in one session with identical arguments, with no success of that command and nothing changed in between: no edit, and no other command that could have changed files (a script, an install, a move). Dropped as waiting if the same line then passes with nothing changed; never dropped because it passed after something was done.
signals.title: Retry loop
signals.why: The failure output did not tell the agent what to do, so it kept guessing.

signals.attribution: The normalized command, and the files edited between the runs (the 3 most edited, split evenly).
signals.description: Within one turn the agent ran the same command 4 or more times, each run after a file change since the previous one, every run failed as an ordinary failure, and the turn ended with the command still failing.
signals.title: No convergence
signals.why: Edit, run, red, again and again without ever going green: the agent could not work out what the check wants.

signals.attribution: The file the tool targeted, or the normalized command for shell calls.
signals.description: The human declined a tool call the agent proposed. Declining a plan or a question is not counted.
signals.title: Tool call declined
signals.why: The agent wanted to do something a human considered wrong or unsafe here.

signals.attribution: The target of the agent's most recent tool call in that turn.
signals.description: The human interrupted the agent after it had made at least one tool call in the turn. The interrupt that accompanies a declined tool call is not counted again.
signals.title: User interrupt
signals.why: The human saw the agent going wrong and stopped it.

signals.description: An edit failed because the text to replace was not found in the file, or matched several places.
signals.title: Edit miss
signals.why: The agent's picture of the file was wrong, or the file has repeated blocks that are hard to target; each miss costs a re-read and a retry.

signals.description: An edit exactly undid an earlier successful edit to the same file in the same session, or a write restored an earlier version of the file. Taking out lines that were only added and then run successfully (a debug print) is not counted.
signals.title: Edit reverted
signals.why: Work on this file went in a circle.

signals.attribution: The normalized command. Ordinary failures are also attributed to repo files named on the command line; setup/invocation errors are not (the files are not the cause).
signals.description: A shell command failed: it exited non-zero or, where the exit status belongs to a pipe or a later step, its own output says so. Setup and invocation errors (command not found, missing module, bad arguments, …) and environment failures (a service that is not running, missing credentials, an unset variable) count fully; ordinary failures, such as a test that fails, count at 0.3. A red run followed by an edit and a green run of the same job is dropped; one that passed only after a setup step, with no file edited, is kept in full. Read-only inspection commands (ls, grep, …) are ignored.
signals.title: Command failure
signals.why: Agents guess how to build, test and run things; a wrong guess burns a round trip every session until the right command is written down.

signals.attribution: The file, from git history. Never raises confidence on its own.
signals.description: A commit attributed to an agent changed a file, and the next commit touching that file, made by a human within the rework window, rewrote lines the agent commit had written or is described as a fix or revert. A human continuing work elsewhere in the file does not count.
signals.title: Human rework (git)
signals.why: Agent output on this file needed a human follow-up soon after it landed.

signals.description: One file received 6 or more successful edits within a single turn in which something also went wrong: an edit miss, a stale edit or a reverted edit on that file, or a failed command or retry loop in the turn. Not recorded next to a no-convergence event of the same turn that names the file.
signals.title: Edit thrash
signals.why: Many small edits to one file in one go usually means trial and error rather than a plan. Weak signal on its own.

signals.attribution: The file the tool targeted, or the normalized shell command (the step most likely to have been refused).
signals.description: A tool call was refused by permission settings, a hook or a safety check before it ran. No human was asked, and the command or edit never happened.
signals.title: Permission denied
signals.why: The agent wanted to do something the setup does not allow. Either the allow-list is missing a routine command, or the agent does not know the boundary.

signals.description: An edit or write was refused because the file had not been read first, or changed on disk after it was read.
signals.title: Stale edit
signals.why: Something else (formatter, code generator, watcher, another agent) rewrites this file, or the agent edits it blind.

signals.attribution: Split evenly over the files edited in the preceding turn (the 5 most recent).
signals.description: A human prompt that is worded like a correction but is not corroborated by behaviour (the agent had changed nothing, or the human names no changed file and the agent did not go back to what it had changed), or that only contains two or more weaker cues. It may be an ordinary follow-up request.
signals.title: Probable correction
signals.why: Possibly a redirect by a human. Kept apart from corrections so that a guess never inflates their count; never quoted, never the basis of a recommendation.

signals.description: A read was refused because the file exceeds what the harness returns in one piece.
signals.title: File too large to read
signals.why: The agent has to page through the file or search it blind, in every session.

signals.attribution: The non-existent path (so repeated wrong guesses add up).
signals.description: The agent tried to read or edit a path that does not exist. A read of a missing file that the agent then creates in the same session is not recorded.
signals.title: Path miss
signals.why: The agent expected something to live here; the layout or naming misled it.

signals.attribution: The file or directory that was searched.
signals.description: A Grep or Glob search returned nothing. A search that only confirms a name is free before the agent creates it is not recorded.
signals.title: Search miss
signals.why: The agent looked for a name that is not there; repeated misses in one place point at vocabulary the codebase does not use.

signals.description: The same range of a file was read 3 or more times in one session with no successful edit to it in between.
signals.title: Read loop
signals.why: The agent keeps going back to this file without making progress. Weak signal.
